wiki-iran.standing: Wikipedia's article on Iran, and how many people open it each day. Readership of a country page tracks the days that country becomes the world's story, so the count is a rough register of global attention rather than of events themselves.
wiki-iran.recent: The peak on 25 August came as Washington widened sanctions under "Operation Economic Outcast", designating six Banque Misr branches out of dollar access, and Iran vowed to resist. Attention held through Iran's terms for Hormuz transit and the US strike on two IRGC launchers at Larak Island on 30 August, justified as pre-empting a mining of the strait.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The strait did the work. Brent peaked at $105.30 on Jul 23 with Hormuz shut, through which a fifth of the world's oil transits, then fell back once Hormuz was declared open and tankers resumed crossing. Washington's move on Venezuelan crude, 65 billion barrels of reserves, added supply to the far side of the trade.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of American light sweet crude, the benchmark US oil is sold against and the reference for North American refiners. It moves on supply and demand shifts, and fuel and freight costs follow it.
wti.recent: Crude has fallen roughly 14% over the window despite the Hormuz closure, where traffic dropped to single digits as the 60-day US-Iran deadline expired — China cut oil imports 45%, absorbing the chokepoint through inventory before price. Barrels are also rerouting, with Washington negotiating a stake in Venezuela's fields.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline hub in Louisiana. It prices power generation, heating and fertiliser feedstock across North America, and it anchors what American LNG costs the buyers who ship it abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: US gas has drifted down to $2.70 even as the global picture tightened: EU storage sits near 64% heading into winter, Delhi raised compressed natural gas ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on surging LNG prices, and Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts after an RLNG cargo delay. The series peaked at $3.34 on Jun 30 and bottomed at $2.56 on Aug 7.

wheat.standing: The world benchmark price for a metric ton of milling wheat, the grain behind bread, flour and much of the world's animal feed. It moves on harvests, export policy and war in the countries that grow the surplus, and food bills follow it.
wheat.recent: The rise is a policy story as much as a harvest one. Sindh will import 5 million tons of wheat after withdrawing its support price, a withdrawal that cut acreage and turned a producing province into a buyer. Bakers in Nairobi are meanwhile substituting cassava and sorghum flour for imported wheat.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple calorie for roughly half the planet. It is thinly traded relative to how many people eat it, so a single exporter's ban or a monsoon failure moves the price for importers everywhere.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen 17.7% over the window and sits at $464 a tonne, down sharply from the $563.80 peak of Aug 2024 and closer to the $330.60 floor of Oct 2025. The input does not name the supply or policy change behind the decline.

copper.standing: The benchmark price for refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Grids, motors, buildings and cables all bid for the same supply, so its price tracks how fast the world is wiring itself.
copper.recent: Copper set a record 13,550 $/mt in Jun 2026, roughly half again above its Dec 2024 low of 8,910. Demand for grid and vehicle hardware sits behind the climb: transformer designs are being reworked for AI load, and EV charging build-outs compete for the same metal. In Zambia, a top producer, Hakainde Hichilema won a second term with 60% of the vote.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself. It is the reference rate under mortgages, corporate loans and asset prices everywhere, so when it rises the cost of borrowing rises with it.
us-10y.recent: Yields have climbed through the summer as Treasury's sanctions campaign and a contested Fed succession pulled at the market at once: Bessent's "Economic Outcast" programme extended dollar-clearing penalties to third-country banks, and Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced expectations for the path of rates. The thirty-year reached 5.3%, a 2007 level.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Pensions, index funds and corporate valuations worldwide are benchmarked against it.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its two-month peak of 7,799 reached on Aug 13, up 1.34% over the window. The gains ran through AI hardware: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers, financing the demand it books as revenue, while cheaper inference tools eroded the pricing power of top-end models. Retail pulled the other way after Walmart's results.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. Chipmakers, software and platform companies dominate it, so it moves as a barometer of how much the market will pay for technology growth.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its June high after a July trough, with the sector's largest names moving on their own news rather than a common shock. Nvidia guided to $108bn in revenue next quarter, while also backstopping $230 billion in customer lease obligations and pledging $500 billion to its own buyers — financing that returns to it as sales. Meta settled child-safety claims for $17.1bn, roughly 1% of its stock value.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across the United States, surveyed weekly. It follows crude and refining margins with a lag, and it is the price through which oil markets reach household budgets and politics.
us-gas-retail.recent: The window's pressure is on refining, not crude. Ukrainian drones struck the Samara refinery, Moscow capped station sales at 30 litres, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved" as Russia moved to import fuel and lower standards. US retail sits at $4.085, down 1.5% over the series and below the Jun 8 high of $4.146.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered to the Dutch TTF hub, Europe's benchmark for pipeline and LNG supply. It sets what the continent's households, power stations and fertiliser plants pay, and competes with Asian buyers for the same cargoes.
natgas-ttf.recent: Gas has climbed roughly 47% off its December low as Europe heads toward winter with storage near 64%, well below where it should be. Cargoes are being bid away by Asian buyers — Delhi raised compressed natural gas ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on surging LNG prices — while Nord Stream stays a crime scene, with a second suspect arrested in Croatia.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of market fear.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down about 8% over the window and sits near the low of 14.25 reached on 14 August, well below the 22.22 peak of 10 June. The feed does not identify what drove the decline.

fx-pkr.standing: Pakistan's currency, quoted against the dollar. The country imports its fuel, gas and much of its wheat, so the rate sets the cost of the energy bill and the food bill, and it shapes the size of every dollar debt repayment.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee drifted to a 30-day low as the import bill kept its pressure on. Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts after a delayed RLNG cargo, Sindh moved to import 5 million tons of wheat after withdrawing its support price, and oil marketing companies keep building fuel pumps rather than chargers, leaving refined-product imports intact.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted per US dollar. Africa's largest oil producer earns dollars from crude and spends them on imported fuel and food, so the naira transmits oil revenue, central-bank reserves and import bills into every domestic price.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed through August as Nigeria's foreign reserves hit a 20-year high, a run Moody's rewarded when it scored Abuja's austerity on 29 August. FTSE Russell will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on 21 September, restoring frontier status and the index flows that follow it. The low of 1,342 came on 29 August.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar. The country imports most of its wheat and fuel, and services heavy external debt, so the rate sets the price of bread and borrowing for more than 100 million people.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has been steady across the month, ending near 50.68 after a high of 51.16 on Aug 2 and a low of 49.56 on Aug 8. On Aug 28 the US cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system, the sharpest external pressure in the window.

fx-try.standing: The exchange rate of Turkey's currency against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the cost of imported energy, food and machinery for a large industrial economy that buys most of its fuel abroad.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low against the dollar through a month of security commitments abroad: Turkey summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships in the Black Sea, ran a ten-day operation against pirates off Somalia, and on 31 August hosted the first meeting of the Mecca defence pact committee in Istanbul.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar. It sets the import bill for a country that buys its fuel, wheat and cotton abroad and pays for them in dollars, while its garment exports and worker remittances are what earn those dollars back.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka held in a narrow band, near 123 to the dollar, ranging only between 124 on Aug 7 and 122 on Aug 19. Nothing in the month's news — the election of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as president, the confirmed purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighters — moved it beyond that range.

fx-idr.standing: The currency of Southeast Asia's largest economy, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Indonesia funds itself heavily in foreign currency and exports commodities priced in dollars, which makes the rate a gauge of both.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah firmed about 1.6% over the month, from 18,040 on Aug 4 to 17,650 on Aug 21 before easing to 17,750. The month's news was structural rather than monetary: Prabowo tightening the state's grip on the economy through cooperatives, a ruling that gig drivers are "partners" rather than employees, and RCEP's persistent gap between integrated goods trade and capital.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Lebanon's economy runs largely on dollars, so the rate sets the real value of salaries, savings and imported food and fuel for anyone paid in local currency.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound drifted from 89,250 on Aug 3 to 89,980 on Aug 31, a slow slide against the dollar rather than a break. It moved through a month in which Lebanon's health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350, Israeli strikes killed 11, and troops occupied Christian villages in the border zone.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted against the dollar and managed by the People's Bank of China within a daily band rather than left to float freely. Its level sets the price of the world's largest manufacturing base's exports.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to 6.723 after a 6.755 high on Aug 4, moving little while Washington pressed the G20 to push Beijing to curb its export surplus and boost domestic demand. Trade policy, not currency markets, carried the argument.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate between India's rupee and the US dollar. India imports most of its crude oil and pays for it in dollars, so a weaker rupee feeds straight into fuel, freight and the cost of imported energy at home.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee held in a narrow band, near 95.77 on Aug 20 and 95.05 on Aug 5, while India worked around US tariff pressure: Modi met Putin at the Bishkek summit Washington skipped, and Uzbekistan agreed to supply nuclear fuel outside Moscow's orbit with a $5 billion bilateral trade target by 2030. Imported energy costs still bit — Delhi's CNG jumped ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It is the price of exposure to Latin America's largest economy, and it moves on commodity earnings, interest-rate policy and confidence in Brasília.
fx-brl.recent: The real drifted about 2% weaker over the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a high of 5.222 on Aug 15, and sat at 5.194 by month-end. The collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe put Brazilian bank supervision in question late in the period, while Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast that Lula called a "passport.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos it takes to buy one US dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Latin America — freely floating and liquid around the clock, which makes it a standing proxy for emerging-market and US trade risk.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso firmed across the month, from 17.35 to the dollar on Aug 2 to a high of 16.92 on Aug 21, before easing back to 17.02 — a move of under two percent, and one no single event accounts for.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, the world's most traded currency pair. It prices everything the euro area buys abroad — oil, gas and shipping are invoiced in dollars — so a weaker euro raises import costs across twenty economies.
fx-eur.recent: The euro slid to 0.8556 on Aug 20 before recovering to 0.8627, a drift of under half a percent across the month. EU gas storage sitting near 64% leaves Europe bidding for LNG cargoes on a global spot market priced in dollars, and Brussels spent the month on Russia policy — four member states pushing to unlock frozen assets, Germany preparing its own sanctions.

fx-jpy.standing: The price of a dollar in yen, and the most traded currency pair in Asia. Japan imports nearly all its energy in dollars, so a weaker yen raises the cost of every barrel, cargo and component landing in the country.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen broke 160 per dollar on Monday, its weakest of the month against 156.5 on Aug 3, putting the Ministry of Finance on intervention watch. The Bank of Japan's rate gap with the Fed is the engine, and spot intervention does not close it. Japanese importers are paying for energy in dollars as crude climbs.

fx-rub.standing: Russia's currency, priced against the dollar. It is the clearest live gauge of what sanctions, oil revenue and capital controls are doing to the Russian economy, and it sets the cost of every import a Russian household buys.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid to 86.15 on Aug 29 from 79.26 on Aug 2 as the sanctions net tightened: Germany began preparing national measures after a bomb-rigged drone landed near a cargo plane at Leipzig, and a Georgian refinery at Kulevi took its first Libyan cargo in place of Russian crude. Households moved 4.2 trillion rubles into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, and the most heavily traded currency on the African continent. It is a proxy for emerging-market risk appetite and for the metals South Africa exports, so it moves on both foreign capital flows and commodity prices.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through August, reaching 15.92 on Aug 26 before easing to 16.18. The month's news from Pretoria was governance rather than markets: the diversion of 12 million rand for covert operations, R88.6bn sitting unclaimed in dormant accounts and pensions, and 40,000 students improperly funded R5.1 billion.

btc.standing: The first cryptocurrency and the largest by market value, traded around the clock on exchanges worldwide. It has no yield and no issuer, so its price is set purely by what buyers will pay, which makes it one of the most volatile assets that regulated institutions now hold.
btc.recent: The rally from about $62,000 to above $77,000 was a short squeeze rather than a leveraged bid: CME futures open interest climbed from roughly 87,000 to 122,000 BTC as traders positioned around Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million in the same stretch.

eth.standing: The native token of Ethereum, the largest programmable blockchain, used to pay for transactions and to secure the network. Its price tracks demand for the settlement layer under most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised finance.
eth.recent: Ether rose with a wave of US policy movement: the SEC proposed its first major crypto rulebook on 18 August, Trump pushed Congress on the Clarity Act at a White House event the next day, and Treasury buybacks lifted risk appetite as bitcoin climbed above $68,000. The high of $2,515 came on 22 Aug.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold in a London vault, so its price tracks the metal per troy ounce. It trades around the clock, which makes it a live read on where safe-haven demand is going when other gold markets are closed.
paxg.recent: The metal ran from $4,045 on Aug 2 to a $4,672 peak on Aug 25, days before Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech that gold and Bitcoin were both pricing, a test of Fed independence. Physical demand showed the same pull: in Kassala, Sudan, street dealers outbid the licensed market until traders shut shop.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The general-purpose Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence, and one of the site's most-read technology pages. Its daily readership is a rough gauge of how far AI has pushed past the trade press into ordinary public attention.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership has drifted down from its 14 August peak to 18,060 views a day. The stories through the window were industrial rather than dramatic: Nvidia backstopping $230 billion in customer lease obligations, Meta scrapping planned AI-driven cuts of up to 60% in some teams, and a US court voiding the Pentagon's ban on Anthropic.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and the daily count of people reading it. Attention to a country page tracks what the world is being told about it, so the series rises with wars, sanctions and deployments rather than with anything inside the encyclopedia.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership climbed through a month in which Russia's war widened on two fronts. A strike on an arms depot near Kyiv set off stored shells and killed 37, and Moscow claims it destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants. Beyond Ukraine, Niger's army formally asked Moscow to put down its own mutiny, and Germany began preparing sanctions after a bomb-rigged drone landed at Leipzig.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a nuclear-armed state of some 250 million people. Attention here tracks what the wider world is being told about South Asia, and spikes when the country's politics, military or disasters break internationally.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The peak on Aug 14 preceded the month's biggest Pakistan story: a nursery fire at Pims in Islamabad that killed 14 newborns on Aug 26, and a payout of 5 million rupees per family. Imran Khan was returned to jail after hospital checks on Aug 21, and army chief Asim Munir travelled to Tehran on Aug 24, a trip Pakistan denies was made for Trump.

wiki-china.standing: The English Wikipedia article on China, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership of a country page tracks the days that country becomes the story rather than the background — a rough public attention meter, unfiltered by any newsroom.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak sits inside a run of stories in which China is the counterparty rather than the subject: Washington asked the G20 to press Beijing to shrink its export surplus and consume more at home, Bangladesh confirmed a purchase of J-10CE fighters, and Nigeria pitched oilfields to Chinese capital at a Shandong trade fair.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The Wikipedia page for the sea lane between Iran and Oman that links the Gulf to open ocean. Readership rises when the strait is threatened, which makes it a rough gauge of how widely a shipping crisis has registered with the public.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The 18 August peak followed a vessel being struck by an unknown projectile in the strait, days after traffic fell to single digits when the 60-day deadline for the US-Iran MoU expired. Attention has stayed elevated since: Iran now says transit requires Tehran's permission, and 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India — a proxy for how much of the world is looking up the country at once. It rises when India is doing something abroad, and when something happens to Indians abroad.
wiki-india.recent: The mid-August peak sat with the row over US envoy Sergio Gor calling J&K an "important part of India", which Pakistan summoned him over, and Washington citing India on voter IDs. Readership eased after, then held through the Nepal floods that left 288 Indians missing and India airlifting aid to Kathmandu.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of Wikipedia's article on Ukraine, a proxy for how many people worldwide are trying to orient themselves on the country. It rises when the war forces a general audience to look something up.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv, where Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023, and Britain cleared MBDA to share SCALP missile component data with France and Ukraine. Attention held through the strike on an arms depot near Kyiv, whose death toll rose to 38, and Turkey's summons of Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to a fraction of its 90-day baseline as Iran declared that transit requires Tehran's permission and the IRGC claimed a veto over the strait. US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday over sea-mine preparations. Some 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships; Delhi CNG rose ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits near a fifth below where it was in early June, and the Houthi campaign is why. A Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, and the group said it attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia the same day; Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Yemen's Saada the same day.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic sits near the bottom of its range after Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, including a vessel struck off Saudi Arabia on 24 August and an earlier attack that injured Pakistani nationals. Transits peaked at 57 a day on 11 August before falling back to 37, roughly the level the canal has held through the shipping disruption.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run below its own 90-day baseline, thinning from the June peak with no weather behind it — waves have stayed near flat. The pressure has been upstream: shipping in Hormuz has slowed to a near halt, and Houthi missiles hit a Saudi tanker off Yanbu, cutting the volume of tankers that reach Malacca at all.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running close to its own 90-day baseline, down 2.9%, with no weather alert and waves under 2 metres — the swings in the series are counting artefacts rather than closures. Washington is pressing the G20 to curb China's export surplus and Trump plans chip tariffs, but neither has yet shown up in vessel counts through the strait.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running about 13 percent below their 90-day baseline, at 28 vessels a day against a July 13 high of 83. The canal authority moved to cap daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño, the weather pattern that drains the lake the locks depend on. Separately, CK Hutchison is seeking HK$11.7b from Panama over a dispute about the canal's ports.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has run below its 90-day baseline as strikes at sea spread: three Greek vessels burned in the Black Sea in three days in August, and Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish-operated ships. Neutral flags confer no protection on the routes both navies now treat as targets, and grain and fuel transit the straits.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic is down 5.7% against its own 90-day baseline, with no weather to explain it — waves peaked at 0.6m. The window covers Washington's "Operation Economic Outcast", which named nearly 60 entities and cut six Banque Misr branches off from US dollars, and Tehran's admission that foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has run about a fifteenth below its 90-day baseline, with the window's high of 186 vessels on Aug 1 falling to 126 just two days later before settling near 154. Seas stayed calm, peaking at 2 metres, and nothing in the record explains the swing.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline through August, running about 84 vessels a day after a swing from 68 on 27 July to 123 on 31 July. Attacks on shipping continued in the corridors this route bypasses: a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, and Hormuz traffic fell to single digits in mid-August.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, roughly 97 percent below its own 90-day baseline, after strikes at sea spread far enough that Turkey summoned Ukraine's ambassador over attacks on Turkish-operated ships in the Black Sea. Neutral flags no longer protect hulls on routes both navies treat as targets, and commercial operators have stopped sailing.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index reached 11,260 on Aug 26 as Riyadh moved on two fronts: a nuclear deal submitted to Congress that skips an enrichment ban and the Additional Protocol, and the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Turkey, whose first committee met in Istanbul. It has since slipped 0.9% to 11,160.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after a month of Turkish foreign-policy escalation: Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships in the Black Sea, sought an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case, and hosted the first Mecca Pact defence committee in Istanbul. None of it dented the market.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index fell after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Pressure continued on 28 August as Bessent targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its 26 August peak of 1749 to 1726, a slide that coincided with prosecutors charging former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing some $40 million in assets on 27 August. The window still leaves it above its 1 July low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth off its June low as Prabowo pushed the state deeper into the economy, routing activity through cooperatives, and it reached its high on Aug 21. It has drifted since, easing again on the latest session.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar, a level that put the Ministry of Finance on intervention watch and left Japanese importers paying for energy in dollars. The index is down on the day and slightly below where it stood two months ago, well off its 72,370 high of Jun 25 and above the 61,430 low of Jul 29.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has round-tripped: after the low on Jun 26 it recovered to 25,410, roughly where it began the window. The nearest pressure is trade — the US is asking the G20 to press Beijing to curb its export surplus and lift domestic demand, a coalition-building step ahead of tariff coordination.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index has drifted down roughly 3% over the quarter from its 22 June high of 4,163, and sits near 3,944 after a 17 July low of 3,764. Washington is now asking the G20 to press Beijing to curb its export surplus and lift domestic demand, and Wang Yi has told Washington to "remove disruptions" before a summit.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea hiked rates to 3.00% on 27 August, tightening into a chip-export cycle that carries a disproportionate share of national output while the won stays weak. The index sits roughly a quarter below its 22 June high of 9115, with the trough at 5594 on 30 July. President Lee Jae Myung's reshuffle promoted Lee Hyoung-il to finance minister, signalling continuity.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after an Aug 6 high of 78950, with Indian corporate leadership and trade news setting the tone: HDFC Bank's chief executive declined a third term, leaving the country's largest private lender facing an RBI-supervised succession, while India and Uzbekistan set a $5 billion bilateral trade target for 2030 alongside a nuclear fuel supply deal outside Moscow's orbit.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed steadily since June, reaching 5,768 on Aug 17 before easing. Singapore's role as a trade and finance conduit ran through the period: a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties, and crypto card spending in the city tripled to $1.04 billion.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a slide to 39,930 on Jul 30 and a recovery since. August brought pressure from both sides of the risk: Taiwan indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager over AI server smuggling, and Xiaomi launched its own Xring O3 chip in a direct challenge to Qualcomm.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 38-day range, roughly 3 percent above the 1,541 low of Jun 23, after peaking at 1,639 on Jul 17 — but it fell 3 percent on the latest session. Nothing in the available reporting from Bangkok explains that single-day drop.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its range, close to the 5,769 low of May 29 and well below the 6,404 peak of July 17. The fall came alongside the Senate impeachment proceedings in Manila, where a former disbursing officer testified that Duterte ordered a P125-million transfer of confidential funds.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up about 4% over the past two months and only a fraction below the Aug 6 high of 9,272. Little of the move traces to a single domestic event: the market was reported falling ahead of inflation data on Aug 18, and the sharpest Australian corporate news of the period was KPMG cutting 27 partners and 360 staff.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to 118,200 on 28 August, its highest in the 65-day window and about 2.7% above the 23 July low of 108,300. The coverage in this period concerns South African governance and public finance rather than listed companies, and does not explain the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index dipped to its low on Aug 18 as the fraud probe that brought down Bank Master raised questions about supervisory failure in Brazilian banking, then recovered most of the ground into late August. Petrobras signs of oil off the Amazon coast, which Lula called a "passport," supported the energy side of the index.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down about 5% over the past three months, from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a low of 63,930 on Aug 18, and sits near 65,480. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the past three months, off its 22 July high of 3,380,000 and near the 19 August low of 2,874,000. The one Buenos Aires story in the window is an Interpol operation that dismantled a fraud network, with 58 arrested and 196 identified — nothing that explains the move in equities.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index climbed through the summer and peaked at 36,960 on Aug 25, days after trade talks with Washington collapsed and Ottawa answered new US tariffs with a 'dollar-for-dollar' list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles. Ontario Premier Doug Ford has backed retaliation, threatening to cut power exports.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high of 7799 after a run from 7267 on Jun 10, with US policy actions dominating the period: Treasury designated Banque Misr and promised another bank this week, US forces struck IRGC launchers on Larak Island, and Washington took majority control of Venezuela's PDVSA and its 65 billion barrels.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, roughly 3.8% above where it started the window and just short of the 10,910 high set on Jul 29. Nothing in the London news flow explains the move; the period's UK headlines were Russia's warnings over British aid to Ukraine and the impostor messages sent to Prime Minister Burnham.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index climbed to a series high of 26570 on Aug 28, up 5.9% over the window, as Berlin moved towards sanctioning Russia over the Leipzig airport drone attack and Brussels prepared what Kallas calls the broadest package yet. Sanctions-exposed firms are the ones carrying that risk.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index rose to 8401, roughly 2.6% above where it sat in June, after touching 8726 on Aug 10. Paris-listed aerospace had a busy month: the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three rocket startups, passing over Ariane's own MaiaSpace, and said it would adapt Ariane 6 for nuclear-powered Argonaut landers.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up around 7% over the window, with the high on Aug 13 and the low back on May 29. The material here does not explain the move.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed roughly a tenth over the past three months, from its low on Jun 10 to a peak of 20210 on Aug 11, and it has held near that level since. The input offers nothing on what drove the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index has climbed about 5.6% over the window, reaching a high of 53,720 on Aug 7 after a low of 49,780 on Jun 1, and closing at 52,620 on Aug 28. Nothing in the material at hand explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up about 6.6% over the period, having climbed from a low of 13,220 on Jun 3 to a high of 14,630 on Aug 10 before easing to 14,400. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index closed at its 66-day high on 28 August, up about 7 percent from its 10 June low. Nothing in the available material explains the climb.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with every signal about the direction of US monetary policy.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The market swung on how hawkish the Fed sounded. Odds of no change peaked at 75 on Aug 15, then fell after minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and the contract sits at 47. Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, which bitcoin and gold were already pricing, kept the question open.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia biography of the sitting US president, and one of the most-read political pages in any language. Its daily readership rises whenever an American decision lands abroad, which makes it a rough gauge of how far a presidency is reaching.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 26 August peak followed the Saudi 123 agreement, which left enrichment unbanned and awaits Saudi recognition of Israel. Readership stayed high through the war-aims posts on Iran, Trump's declaration that Hormuz was clear, and his request that regulators punish NBC anchor Kristen Welker.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A crypto token pegged to a national currency, usually the dollar, and backed by reserves held off-chain. It is the settlement layer most crypto trading runs on, and the form in which banks and card networks are now moving deposits.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Attention tracked stablecoins moving from crypto into ordinary banking. Standard Chartered began distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, Shinhan started building won rails with a card network, and 39 state banking associations announced a rival chain to defend deposits. Crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country itself rather than any single story about it.
wiki-united-states.recent: Attention tracked the widening confrontation with Iran: the 28 August peak came as Washington unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" against banks handling Iranian trade and declared Hormuz open, with Tehran conceding its foreign trade had shrunk by more than a third. US forces then struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The pageview count for Wikipedia's Bitcoin article, a rough gauge of how many people are looking the asset up rather than trading it. Attention tends to arrive with price moves, and it arrives late.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Readership tracked Bitcoin's run from about $62,000 to above $77,000 in days, peaking on Aug 24 as the surge to $80,020 — up 23.7% in a week — turned out to be a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally. CME futures open interest climbed from roughly 87,000 to 122,000 BTC, and the firms that made the most were market makers taking no view on price.

wiki-nepal.standing: The Wikipedia article on Nepal, a Himalayan republic of about 30 million between India and China, whose rivers drain the world's highest mountains. Readership of it rises when the country enters the news, usually through earthquake, flood or a change of government.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between banks. It is the base cost of dollar credit, and mortgages, corporate borrowing and the price of the dollar abroad all take their cue from it.
fed-funds.recent: The rate has been held at 3.75% since December 2025, down from 5.5% in August 2024, but the direction of travel has reversed: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and markets now favor a September hike. Attention has centred on Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks to park cash overnight, and the floor under euro-zone borrowing costs. It sets what savers earn and what mortgages, business loans and government debt cost across the currency bloc.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate sits at 2.25%, down from 3.75% in Aug 2024 and a quarter-point above the Jun 2025 low of 2%, and the input does not explain the latest move. Elsewhere the direction has turned: the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00%, and Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is looking for work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, down from the 4.5% high reached in November 2025 and close to the 4% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on party manoeuvring rather than on anything the candidate's own campaign publishes.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.recent: The contract slid from 28% on Aug 1 to 16%, its low, over a month in which the venue itself was under strain rather than the field. South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting Polymarket access, a Ninth Circuit ruling confirmed state powers over prediction markets, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer, where a single refinery-and-import balance sets the pump price for over 200 million people, and where fuel policy is the central fact of national politics.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention tracked a policy and security run rather than one event: Atiku Abubakar's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy in 2027 drew an APC accusation of desperation, Tinubu suspended three permanent secretaries over a fake agency, and Abuja moved to tighten petrol import rules after imports hit 43% of July supply.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia becomes the Democratic presidential nominee. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on primary field news rather than on polling alone.
poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.recent: The series drifted between 14 and 17 through August with no candidate news behind it; the month's news about this market was regulatory rather than electoral. A Ninth Circuit ruling on 28 August held that sports bets are not "swaps", handing states power over prediction markets, and Connecticut filed suit against Kalshi.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the terminal that handles the bulk of its crude exports, before the year ends. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks how far the war has moved toward Iran's oil.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: The contract has drifted down through August even as fighting continued, hitting 6 on Aug 29 before edging back to 9. Iran set terms for Hormuz transit requiring Tehran's permission, and US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island on Sunday over sea mines — pressure aimed at the strait, not at seizing an export terminal.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on which party wins the most seats in Russia's next State Duma election. United Russia is the governing party, and the price is what traders will pay for the proposition that it holds its parliamentary majority.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The price firmed as the war closed off any off-ramp: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead on 27 August, and the strikes kept coming — a depot blast near Bucha that killed 37, a strike on Belgorod that killed two including a 16-year-old, and Russia's claim that it destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants. The contract moved from 62 on 1 August to 75 on 30 August.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance becomes the next US president. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how the field of likely 2028 candidates is being read rather than any poll.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The contract drifted from 20% on Aug 1 to 25% on Aug 30, its high for the month. Nothing in the month's news explains the shift; the prediction-market stories of the period were about the venues rather than the race — a White House aide fined for betting on Trump's speeches, and a Ninth Circuit ruling curbing Kalshi.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before the end of 2026. Traders price the chance of an exit by any route — resignation, removal, death or a scheduled handover — so it reads as a market gauge of Kremlin stability.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The price has drifted down through August as the war ground on without any crack in Moscow's position: Kremlin sources declared peace talks dead, Russia claimed strikes on Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants, and a strike on an arms depot near Bucha killed 37. Odds slipped from 9% on Aug 1 to 7%.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington lifts its naval blockade of Iran by a set date. Traders price it in cents on the dollar; the number is what people are betting, not a forecast, and it moves with each strike, sanction and truce signal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The odds fell from 86 on Aug 8 to 22 as escalation replaced settlement: Treasury's "Operation Economic Outcast" cut six Banque Misr branches off from US dollar access, US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, and Iran declared that Hormuz transit now requires Tehran's permission.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether US forces mount a ground invasion of Iran. It is not a forecast but a price traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on the gap between American strikes and American troops.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The price fell through August as Washington's pressure stayed financial rather than territorial: "Operation Economic Outcast" designated six Banque Misr branches on 28 August, and Hormuz was declared open with 7 tankers crossing. The 28 August low of 13 held even as US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island on Sunday.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A prediction market on whether Brazil's incumbent president wins re-election, priced as what traders will pay for a contract that settles at 100 if he does. It moves on polling, candidate entries and court rulings, not on any forecaster's judgement.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The contract has drifted down through August, from 67% on 2 August to 56% on 30 August, a fall of roughly a fifth. The material in front of us covers the venues rather than the race — a Ninth Circuit ruling curbing Kalshi, a fine for a White House aide who bet on speeches — and none of it explains the move.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A prediction market on whether Israel and Iran will be under a ceasefire by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it tracks how the fighting, the talks and the pressure campaign are being wagered on, not forecast.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The odds sat at 63 on Aug 10 and reached 89 on Aug 25, the week Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent widened sanctions and Iran vowed to resist them, and now stand at 86. The shooting has not stopped: US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, and eight missiles fell over Jordan on Monday.

poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.standing: A prediction market on whether Iran's airspace will be closed to civil aviation by a set date. Traders price the risk that a war shuts the corridor, and the price is what they will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.recent: The price has collapsed from 52% on Aug 2 to 12%, bottoming at 6% on Aug 27, as the fighting moved off Iranian airspace and onto shipping and finance: Hormuz was declared open on Aug 28 with tankers crossing, and Washington's pressure ran through sanctions on Banque Misr rather than air campaigns. The US strike on Larak Island on Aug 30 lifted it only slightly.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran's supreme leader or government is replaced before a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it is a live read on how fragile outsiders think the Islamic Republic's hold on power is.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: Traders have marked the chance down by about a quarter over the month even as the war widened: US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island, Treasury unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" and designated six Banque Misr branches, and Iran admitted foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third. Tehran still set the terms for Hormuz transit.

wiki-tariff.standing: A tax a government charges on imported goods, paid at the border by the importer. It raises the price of foreign products against domestic ones, and the countries hit usually answer with tariffs of their own.
wiki-tariff.recent: The peak on Aug 25 came as Canada matched US tariffs dollar for dollar with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports. Trump then moved to tax chips, a step the Computer & Communications Industry Association puts at a $90 billion annual GDP hit.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, so it tracks how a candidate's chances are being bet on rather than polled.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract climbed from 24% on Aug 1 to 41% on Aug 31, its high for the month. The input carries no Brazilian political news explaining the shift.

poly-will-franois-hollande-win-the-2027-.standing: A prediction market on whether François Hollande, the Socialist who served one term as French president from 2012 to 2017, wins the presidency again in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-franois-hollande-win-the-2027-.recent: The contract has sat between 3% and 4% all month, with no French news moving it. What has moved is the venue: South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting Polymarket access, the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are not "swaps", and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine to settle an insider-trading case over bets on presidential speeches.

poly-israeli-forces-enter-nabatieh-by-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israeli ground forces reach Nabatieh, a city in southern Lebanon, before a set date. It prices how far traders think the Lebanon front will escalate beyond air strikes and border-zone control into occupation of a major town.
poly-israeli-forces-enter-nabatieh-by-se.recent: The price has fallen by roughly three quarters since 27 August, when it sat at 50%. Israeli pressure in south Lebanon has stayed short of a ground advance: soldiers turned back a Catholic aid convoy at a swing gate near Ain Ebel and Rmeish, and force has been applied through permits and blockades rather than manoeuvre. Israel's first West Bank airstrike in ten months killed three in Jenin.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran sign a nuclear agreement before the end of 2026. Traders price it in cents on the dollar, so the number is what people will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: The odds collapsed from 36% on Aug 3 to 11% as the war widened rather than wound down. US forces struck two IRGC launchers on Larak Island, Iran declared Hormuz transit conditional on Tehran's permission, eight missiles fell over Jordan, and Treasury promised another bank designation with truce talks deadlocked.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the odds a chokepoint carrying a fifth of the world's seaborne oil reopens.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders have halved the price since Aug 6, from 62% to 28%, as reopening acquired terms rather than a date. Iran's Gharibabadi said no vessel transits without Tehran's coordination, and the corridor charted with Oman was temporary. A supertanker hit mines in the strait on Aug 31, with 6,000 seafarers still stuck aboard anchored ships.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Bab el-Mandeb strait — the gate between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, and the southern approach to the Suez Canal — will be closed to shipping by a set date. Traders price the risk to that route.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The price has fallen through the month, from 16% on Aug 1 to 5% on Aug 30, with no closure materialising. Polymarket itself was the news: South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access on Aug 18, and on Aug 28 a court ruling confirmed state powers over prediction markets.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, an industrial and monetary metal at once: it is consumed in solar panels, electronics and brazing alloys, and bought as a store of value, so it moves on both factory demand and financial panic.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its $29.81 low on Aug 6 to a $69.42 peak on Aug 28, and no supply, policy or demand event in the input explains the move.
